nodes.label: Photographic
nodes.description: The picture looks like it was actually taken with a camera on film or a sensor, rather than drawn, painted or built inside a computer.
examples: a real photograph of a person on a street
an image with true lens and film behaviour

nodes.label: Fashion editorial
nodes.description: The polished, story-telling fashion photography printed across the pages of a magazine, where an outfit is shown inside a styled scene instead of on a plain catalogue background.
examples: a styled fashion spread shot in a hotel corridor
clothes presented as part of a mood, not as products

nodes.label: High fashion
nodes.description: The most extreme, designer end of fashion imagery: sculptural clothing, dramatic styling and poses that are closer to art direction than to everyday wear.
examples: a couture gown photographed as sculpture
an exaggerated silhouette against a bare set

nodes.label: Lookbook
nodes.description: Clean, repeatable fashion photography made to show a brand's collection clearly, so each full outfit reads plainly from head to toe.
examples: a full-length outfit shot against a plain wall
a seasonal collection shown one look per frame

nodes.label: Advertising campaign
nodes.description: Glossy commercial imagery built to sell something, with deliberate styling, generous space for text and a confident, flattering finish.
examples: a perfume advert with a single striking figure
a billboard image with room for a headline

nodes.label: Beauty
nodes.description: Photography focused tightly on a face, skin, hair or make-up, lit and retouched so that texture and colour on the face are the whole subject.
examples: a close-up of a made-up face on a plain backdrop
glossy skin and lips filling the frame

nodes.label: Street fashion
nodes.description: Real outfits photographed out in the city as people actually wear them, with pavements, traffic and passers-by left in the frame.
examples: an outfit caught crossing a busy pavement
a fashion-week attendee shot outside the venue

nodes.label: Documentary
nodes.description: Pictures that observe something real as it happens, with nothing arranged for the camera, so the moment matters more than the polish.
examples: a family moment recorded without direction
workers photographed mid-task, unposed

nodes.label: Photojournalism
nodes.description: News photography made to report an event honestly, prizing clarity and truthfulness over beauty or styling.
examples: a protest photographed from inside the crowd
a news image that explains an event at a glance

nodes.label: Street photography
nodes.description: Unposed pictures of everyday public life, where the photographer waits for chance arrangements of people, light and gesture to line up.
examples: a stranger caught in a shaft of light between buildings
an accidental gesture framed on a pavement

nodes.label: Studio portrait
nodes.description: A portrait made in a controlled studio, where the background is a plain sweep or backdrop and every light is placed on purpose.
examples: a headshot on a grey seamless backdrop
a figure lit by studio flash against plain paper

nodes.label: Product photography
nodes.description: An object photographed as the subject in its own right, lit evenly and cleanly so the shape, material and finish read without distraction.
examples: a bottle on a plain white sweep
a shoe lit to show its stitching and texture

nodes.label: Fine-art photography
nodes.description: Photography made to hang on a wall rather than to sell or report, where the idea and the print quality matter more than the subject being useful.
examples: a quiet, deliberate image printed for a gallery wall
a conceptual photograph with no commercial purpose

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.description: A quick, casual picture taken without much care about framing or lighting, the way an ordinary person photographs their own life.
examples: a slightly crooked photo of friends at a table
an unplanned picture taken on a phone

nodes.label: Direct-flash snapshot
nodes.description: A picture lit by the camera's own flash pointed straight at the subject, giving bright faces, hard little shadows and a dark background behind them.
examples: a party photo with a bright face and black background
harsh frontal flash on skin at night

nodes.label: Y2K digicam
nodes.description: The look of a cheap digital compact camera from the early 2000s: slightly soft, a bit noisy, over-bright flash and colours that miss slightly.
examples: a night-out photo with blown-out flash and date stamp
a soft, noisy image from a small early digital sensor

nodes.label: Analogue film
nodes.description: The look of a picture taken on photographic film: visible grain, gentle highlight roll-off and colours that come from the film stock rather than a sensor.
examples: a grainy 35mm frame with soft highlights
colour that shifts the way film stock does

nodes.label: Polaroid
nodes.description: The look of an instant photo that developed in your hand: soft focus, milky colours, heavy contrast and often the thick white border of the print.
examples: a washed-out instant print with a white frame
soft, pale colours in a square instant photo

nodes.label: Medium-format film
nodes.description: Film shot on a negative much larger than 35mm, so the picture holds very fine detail and smooth tones with barely any visible grain.
examples: a square film frame with extremely smooth skin tones
a fashion frame with very fine film detail

nodes.label: Expired film
nodes.description: Film that has aged past its date, so colours drift towards odd casts, contrast breaks down and stray streaks of light bleed across the frame.
examples: a green-and-magenta cast with a red light streak
muddy, unpredictable colour on an old roll
nodes.prompt_fragment: expired-film photograph with colour shifts and light leaks
nodes.negative_fragment: no expired-film colour shifts or light leaks

nodes.label: Disposable camera
nodes.description: The rough look of a one-use plastic film camera: fixed focus, heavy grain, a hard built-in flash and slightly crooked framing.
examples: a grainy flash photo from a plastic camera
soft corners and heavy grain on a night-out frame

nodes.label: Super 8
nodes.description: The look of an old home-movie film camera: small grainy frames, jittery movement, faded warm colour and occasional flicker.
examples: a faded, flickering home-movie clip
warm grainy footage that jumps slightly between frames

nodes.label: Cinematic
nodes.description: The picture is treated like a frame from a film: deliberate lighting, wide framing and colour grading that feels staged for a story rather than casually captured.
examples: a moody frame that looks pulled from a feature film
a graded, widescreen-feeling image

nodes.label: Film still
nodes.description: A single frame that looks lifted straight out of a film, complete with the composition, wardrobe and lighting of a real scene.
examples: one frame from a scene, mid-conversation
an image that implies a story before and after it

nodes.label: Film noir
nodes.description: The hard-shadowed crime-film look of the 1940s and 50s: deep blacks, slatted light through blinds, and a dangerous, secretive feeling.
examples: a face half-hidden in blind shadows
a rain-slick street in stark black and white

nodes.label: Music video
nodes.description: The bold, performance-driven look of a music promo, where styling, colour and camera work are pushed harder than in ordinary film.
examples: a saturated performance frame with strong colour lighting
a stylised sequence built around a song

nodes.label: Arthouse
nodes.description: The restrained, unhurried look of festival cinema: quiet framing, natural light and space left for the viewer to sit in the scene.
examples: a still, patient frame of an empty room
a naturally lit scene held longer than usual

nodes.label: Illustration
nodes.description: The image was drawn or painted by hand rather than photographed, so lines, brush marks and flat areas of colour replace real lens and film behaviour.
examples: a hand-drawn figure with visible linework
a painted scene with no photographic detail

nodes.label: Anime
nodes.description: The Japanese animation look: clean outlines, large expressive eyes and flat blocks of colour with hard-edged shading.
examples: a cel-shaded character with crisp outlines
flat colour and sharp shadow edges on a face

model_hints.sd: anime style, cel shaded, clean lineart

nodes.label: Comic art
nodes.description: The printed comic-book look: bold inked outlines, dramatic poses and flat or dotted colour laid inside the lines.
examples: a heavily inked panel with dramatic shadows
flat printed colour inside thick black outlines

nodes.label: Watercolour
nodes.description: A painted look where translucent colour pools and bleeds into wet paper, leaving soft edges and visible paper texture.
examples: soft colour bleeding at the edges of a figure
pale washes with paper grain showing through

nodes.label: Line art
nodes.description: A drawing made almost entirely of outlines, with little or no shading or colour filling them in.
examples: a clean ink outline of a figure
a drawing built only from contour lines

nodes.label: Concept art
nodes.description: Painted design work made to plan a film or game: atmospheric, loosely brushed and focused on mood and world-building rather than fine finish.
examples: a painted city vista made to plan a scene
a loose, atmospheric design painting

nodes.label: 3D render
nodes.description: The image was built and rendered inside 3D software, so surfaces, light and geometry are simulated rather than photographed.
examples: a rendered object with perfectly clean surfaces
simulated light bouncing inside a modelled room

nodes.label: Photoreal CGI
nodes.description: A 3D render made to look as much like a photograph as possible, with believable materials, shadows and lens behaviour.
examples: a rendered interior that could pass for a photo
simulated skin and fabric with photographic detail

nodes.label: Clay render
nodes.description: A 3D render left without textures, so everything appears moulded from the same matte, putty-like material.
examples: an untextured model in soft even light
a scene entirely in matte grey clay

nodes.label: Game engine look
nodes.description: The look of graphics drawn live by a game engine: strong ambient light, crisp surfaces and the slightly clean, weightless feel of real-time rendering.
examples: a screenshot-like frame from a modern game
real-time lighting with very clean surfaces

nodes.label: Calm
nodes.description: The picture feels settled and unhurried, with nothing urgent happening and nothing fighting for attention.
examples: a quiet room with soft light and no movement
a figure sitting still, breathing slowly

nodes.label: Serene
nodes.description: An especially clear, untroubled calm, as though nothing difficult exists just outside the frame.
examples: still water at first light
a face completely at ease

nodes.label: Contemplative
nodes.description: The subject seems to be thinking rather than doing, giving the image an inward, unhurried quality.
examples: a person staring out of a window, unmoving
a gaze turned inward, away from the camera

nodes.label: Energetic
nodes.description: The picture feels fast and alive, as though everything in it is moving or about to move.
examples: a crowd mid-jump at a concert
a body caught in the middle of a fast movement

nodes.label: Playful
nodes.description: The image is light and good-humoured, with a sense of people enjoying themselves and not taking it seriously.
examples: friends laughing mid-joke
a knowing, grinning look straight to camera

nodes.label: Euphoric
nodes.description: An overwhelming, peaking happiness, the feeling of a moment breaking wide open.
examples: arms thrown up in a crowd at the drop
a face lit with uncontainable joy

nodes.label: Moody
nodes.description: A heavy, shadowed feeling where the darkness and the weather of the scene carry as much emotion as the subject does.
examples: a figure half-lost in shadow on a wet street
low light and heavy air over a quiet scene

nodes.label: Melancholic
nodes.description: A gentle, lingering sadness rather than sharp grief, the feeling of missing something that has already gone.
examples: a solitary figure at a rain-streaked window
an empty chair in fading afternoon light

nodes.label: Sombre
nodes.description: A serious, weighty feeling with no lightness in it, the tone of a moment that matters and is not enjoyable.
examples: a hushed room of people standing still
faces set and unsmiling in low light

nodes.label: Mysterious
nodes.description: Something is deliberately withheld, so the viewer is left guessing at who this is or what is about to happen.
examples: a face obscured by shadow or steam
a doorway leading somewhere unseen

nodes.label: Dreamy
nodes.description: The scene feels slightly unreal and softened, as though remembered or imagined rather than witnessed.
examples: a soft, glowing scene with blurred edges
light and colour that feel half-remembered

nodes.label: Ethereal
nodes.description: Light, delicate and barely of this world, as though the subject might dissolve into the light around it.
examples: a figure surrounded by pale glowing haze
a weightless, floating quality to the whole frame

nodes.label: Nostalgic
nodes.description: The image feels like a memory of the past, warm and a little faded, pulling on something the viewer has already lived.
examples: a sun-faded summer afternoon from childhood
a scene that looks recalled rather than seen

nodes.label: Tense
nodes.description: Something feels about to go wrong, so the picture holds a strain that has not yet been released.
examples: two figures facing off in silence
a still frame that feels held breath

nodes.label: Ominous
nodes.description: The picture warns that something bad is coming, even though nothing bad has happened yet.
examples: a dark storm front over an empty road
a long, unlit corridor ahead of the subject

nodes.label: Unsettling
nodes.description: Everything looks almost normal but something is quietly wrong, leaving the viewer uncomfortable without knowing why.
examples: an ordinary room where one thing is out of place
a smile held a moment too long

nodes.label: Intimate
nodes.description: The picture feels close and private, as though the viewer has been let into a moment meant for very few people.
examples: two people sharing a quiet moment inches apart
a small gesture caught very close to the subject

nodes.label: Romantic
nodes.description: Warm, affectionate feeling between people, or a scene lit and framed to feel like falling for someone.
examples: two figures leaning together in warm light
a soft, glowing scene built around affection

nodes.label: Tender
nodes.description: A soft, careful gentleness, the feeling of someone being handled kindly.
examples: a hand resting lightly on a shoulder
a parent holding a sleeping child

nodes.label: Epic
nodes.description: The scene feels enormous and important, dwarfing the people in it and asking to be looked up at.
examples: a lone figure against a vast mountain range
a sweeping view that makes the subject small

nodes.label: Heroic
nodes.description: The subject is presented as strong and admirable, framed and lit so the viewer looks up to them.
examples: a figure standing tall against the sky
a confident stance photographed from below

nodes.label: Dramatic
nodes.description: Everything is heightened: the light, the gesture and the emotion are all pushed well past everyday life.
examples: a face lit by one hard, raking light
a gesture held at its most extreme point

nodes.label: Colour intensity
nodes.description: The family of choices about how strong or washed-out the colours are, from screaming bright to almost grey.
examples: choosing between punchy colour and faded colour
how loud the colours are overall

nodes.label: High saturation
nodes.description: The colours are pushed hard so everything looks bright and intense, well beyond how the eye would see it.
examples: a red jacket that glows off the screen
deep, punchy colour in every part of the frame

nodes.label: Muted
nodes.description: The colours are gently dialled back so nothing shouts, giving a quiet, restrained overall feel.
examples: a soft palette where no colour dominates
clothing and walls in quiet, dusty tones

nodes.label: Desaturated film
nodes.description: Colour is pulled most of the way out, leaving a pale, filmic image that sits just short of black and white.
examples: a nearly grey scene with a hint of skin tone
a bleached, drained film look

nodes.label: Pastel
nodes.description: Pale, milky versions of colours, as though white has been mixed into every one of them.
examples: soft pink and mint against a cream wall
a whole frame in pale, chalky colour

nodes.label: Colour tone
nodes.description: The family of choices about whether the whole picture leans warm like sunlight, cool like shade, or neither.
examples: choosing between a golden or a blue cast
the overall warmth of the image

nodes.label: Warm tone
nodes.description: The whole image leans towards yellows, oranges and reds, so it feels sunlit, cosy or a little nostalgic.
examples: a room bathed in late-afternoon amber
skin and walls both tipped towards gold

nodes.label: Cool tone
nodes.description: The whole image leans towards blues and cyans, so it feels cold, clinical or late in the evening.
examples: a blue-grey street just after sunset
skin tipped slightly towards blue under shade

nodes.label: Neutral tone
nodes.description: Colours sit where the eye expects them, with no push towards warm or cool, so whites simply look white.
examples: daylight-balanced skin tones with no cast
a clean, honest rendering of colour

nodes.label: Colour palette
nodes.description: The family of choices about which colours are allowed in the picture and how they relate to each other.
examples: restricting a scene to two related colours
the set of colours the image is built from

nodes.label: Monochrome
nodes.description: The picture is built from a single colour and its light and dark versions, so no second hue competes with it.
examples: a photograph entirely in greys
a scene rendered only in shades of one blue

nodes.label: Black and white
nodes.description: All colour is removed, leaving only brightness, so the picture is carried by contrast, shape and texture.
examples: a grainy black-and-white street photograph
a portrait with only greys, blacks and whites

nodes.label: Sepia
nodes.description: A single warm brown tone stands in for all colour, the way very old prints have aged.
examples: an aged print in warm brown tones
a portrait toned entirely in soft brown

nodes.label: Cyanotype
nodes.description: A single deep blue tone stands in for all colour, like an old blueprint or sun-printed photograph.
examples: a print entirely in deep prussian blue
a blue-toned image with white highlights

nodes.label: Teal and orange
nodes.description: The familiar cinema grade where skin is pushed warm and orange while the shadows and background go blue-green.
examples: warm faces against a blue-green night street
a graded frame split between amber and teal

nodes.label: Complementary palette
nodes.description: The picture is built from two colours that sit opposite each other on the colour wheel, so each makes the other look stronger.
examples: a red coat against a green hedge
purple light against a yellow wall

nodes.label: Analogous palette
nodes.description: The picture uses colours that sit next to each other on the colour wheel, so the whole frame feels harmonious and unified.
examples: blues and greens throughout a forest scene
yellow into orange into red across one frame

nodes.label: Duotone
nodes.description: The whole picture is printed in just two colours, one carrying the shadows and one the highlights.
examples: a poster in only pink and deep blue
an image mapped to two flat inks

nodes.label: Earth tone
nodes.description: A palette drawn from soil, sand, clay and dry plants: browns, ochres, olive greens and warm greys.
examples: a linen outfit against a clay wall
sand, olive and rust across the whole frame

nodes.label: Neon palette
nodes.description: Electric, glowing colours like lit signage: hot pinks, acid greens and burning blues that look self-illuminated.
examples: magenta and cyan signage reflected on wet tarmac
a face lit by glowing pink and green tubes

nodes.label: Jewel tone
nodes.description: Deep, rich colours named after gemstones: emerald, sapphire, ruby and amethyst, saturated but never glowing.
examples: a deep emerald velvet dress in low light
rich sapphire and ruby across a dark frame

nodes.label: Limited palette
nodes.description: Only a small number of colours are allowed anywhere in the frame, so the image feels deliberate and graphic.
examples: a scene using only red, cream and black
three colours repeated across the whole picture

nodes.label: Split tone
nodes.description: The bright parts of the picture are tinted one colour and the dark parts another, usually warm highlights over cool shadows.
examples: golden highlights with blue-green shadows
a print with warm skin and cold shade

nodes.label: Frame layout
nodes.description: The family of choices about where things are placed inside the rectangle of the picture.
examples: deciding where the subject sits in the frame
the underlying geometry of the arrangement

nodes.label: Rule of thirds
nodes.description: The frame is imagined as a three-by-three grid and the subject is placed on one of those lines instead of dead centre, which usually feels more natural.
examples: a face placed on the left third of the frame
a horizon sitting on the lower third line
nodes.prompt_fragment: composed on the rule of thirds
nodes.negative_fragment: not composed on the rule of thirds

nodes.label: Centred
nodes.description: The subject sits squarely in the middle of the frame, which feels direct, formal and confrontational.
examples: a face placed exactly in the centre
a doorway centred perfectly in the frame

nodes.label: Golden ratio
nodes.description: A slightly tighter cousin of the rule of thirds, placing the subject along a spiral or proportion long used in painting.
examples: a subject placed where a spiral tightens
classical proportion used to place the figure
nodes.negative_fragment: not composed on the golden ratio

nodes.label: Symmetry
nodes.description: The left and right (or top and bottom) halves of the picture mirror each other, giving a formal, deliberate stillness.
examples: a corridor identical on both sides
a face lit and framed perfectly evenly

nodes.label: Asymmetry
nodes.description: The two halves of the frame deliberately do not match, so weight sits to one side and the picture feels alive rather than formal.
examples: a figure pushed hard to one edge
all the visual weight gathered on one side

nodes.label: Diagonal
nodes.description: The main shapes run corner to corner rather than straight across, which makes the picture feel like it is moving.
examples: a staircase cutting across the frame
a body angled from one corner towards another

nodes.label: Triangular
nodes.description: The main elements form a triangle, which holds a group of people or objects together and feels stable.
examples: three figures arranged as a triangle
a seated pose forming a broad pyramid

nodes.label: Radial
nodes.description: Everything spreads outwards from a single point like the spokes of a wheel, pulling the eye to that centre.
examples: a spiral staircase seen from directly above
ceiling beams radiating from one point

nodes.label: Depth cue
nodes.description: The family of devices that make a flat picture feel deep, by layering things from front to back.
examples: putting something close to the lens in front
arranging near, middle and far layers

nodes.label: Leading lines
nodes.description: Lines in the scene, like a road, railing or shadow, run towards the subject and pull the viewer's eye along with them.
examples: a road narrowing towards a distant figure
railings guiding the eye to a face
nodes.prompt_fragment: with leading lines drawing the eye in

nodes.label: Vanishing point
nodes.description: Parallel lines appear to meet at one distant point, which makes the space feel like a tunnel running away from the viewer.
examples: a corridor whose walls converge far away
train tracks meeting at the horizon

nodes.label: Framing within a frame
nodes.description: The subject is seen through an opening in the scene, such as a doorway, window or archway, which boxes them in and adds depth.
examples: a figure seen through a doorway
a face framed by a car window
nodes.prompt_fragment: framed within an opening in the scene

nodes.label: Foreground occlusion
aliases: something in front of the lens
nodes.description: Something sits between the camera and the subject and partly blocks the view, which makes the shot feel observed or stolen.
examples: leaves blurred across the front of the frame
a shoulder cutting into the near edge
nodes.prompt_fragment: with an object partly blocking the foreground

nodes.label: Layered depth
nodes.description: The picture is clearly built from a near layer, a middle layer and a far layer, so the eye travels back through it.
examples: people near, mid and far in one street frame
clear foreground, subject and distant skyline
nodes.prompt_fragment: with clearly layered foreground, middle and background

nodes.label: Reflection
nodes.description: The subject appears in a mirror, window or puddle, doubling them and folding two spaces into one frame.
examples: a figure doubled in a rain puddle
a face caught in a shop window
nodes.prompt_fragment: using a reflection in the composition

nodes.label: Horizon placement
nodes.description: The family of choices about how high or low the horizon line sits, which decides how much sky or ground you see.
examples: choosing how much sky to include
raising or lowering the horizon line

nodes.label: Low horizon
nodes.description: The horizon sits near the bottom of the frame so most of the picture is sky, which makes the scene feel open and airy.
examples: a small figure under an enormous sky
a thin strip of land beneath tall clouds
nodes.prompt_fragment: with a low horizon and a large expanse of sky

nodes.label: High horizon
nodes.description: The horizon sits near the top of the frame so most of the picture is ground or floor, which makes the scene feel grounded and enclosed.
examples: a wide road filling most of the frame
a beach stretching up to a high waterline
nodes.prompt_fragment: with a high horizon and a large expanse of ground

nodes.label: Centred horizon
nodes.description: The horizon cuts the frame in half, giving equal sky and ground, which feels calm, formal and still.
examples: equal sky and sea across the middle
a landscape split evenly in two
nodes.prompt_fragment: with the horizon centred in the frame

nodes.label: Space around the subject
nodes.description: The family of choices about how much empty room is left around the subject, from a lot of air to none at all.
examples: deciding how much empty space surrounds the figure
choosing a tight or an airy crop
nodes.prompt_fragment: with deliberate space around the subject
nodes.negative_fragment: no deliberate spacing around the subject

nodes.label: Negative space
nodes.description: Large parts of the frame are deliberately left empty around the subject, which makes them feel small, calm or isolated.
examples: a figure alone against a huge blank wall
a small subject with plenty of empty air around it
nodes.prompt_fragment: with generous negative space around the subject

nodes.label: Wide negative space
aliases: tiny subject in a big frame
nodes.description: Negative space taken to an extreme: the subject occupies only a small corner of a mostly empty frame.
examples: a lone walker in a vast snowfield
a tiny figure at the base of a blank facade
nodes.prompt_fragment: with vast negative space dwarfing the subject

nodes.label: Tight crop
nodes.description: The frame is cut in hard around the subject, often slicing through them at the edges, so nothing else is visible.
examples: a face cropped through the forehead and chin
fabric filling the entire frame edge to edge

nodes.label: Filled frame
nodes.description: Every part of the picture is occupied by something, leaving no quiet or empty areas for the eye to rest.
examples: a market stall packed corner to corner
a wall of objects filling the whole frame
